dimensions.detail: Name, description, SKILL.md, README, and required env vars (GITHUB_TOKEN, GITHUB_USERNAME) all align with a GitHub integration that lists repos, checks CI, creates issues/repos/PRs, and reads recent activity.

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs only to provide a GitHub PAT and username (via env vars or OpenClaw config) and to restart the gateway; it does not ask for unrelated system credentials or to read arbitrary files. It recommends broad 'repo' scope for private-repo actions — appropriate if you need private-repo writes, but this is a high-privilege scope and should be minimized where possible.

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only), which is low risk, but the packaged JavaScript imports './api' (index.js -> require('./api')) yet no api.* file appears in the provided file manifest. That missing module means the runtime behavior cannot be audited and the package may be incomplete or tampered with.

Note: the recommended 'repo' PAT scope grants full control of private repos — limit scopes to the minimum needed (e.g., public_repo, repo:status, repo:workflow) when feasible.

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be what it says on the surface (it legitimately needs a GitHub token and username), but the packaged code is incomplete: index.js requires a './api' module that is not present in the files provided. That prevents a full audit of what the skill will do with your PAT. Before installing or enabling: 1) Ask the publisher for the missing api module or a complete source bundle and verify there are no external endpoints beyond api.github.com. 2) Use a least-privilege personal access token (avoid broad 'repo' scope unless necessary; use public_repo or more granular scopes where possible). 3) Consider creating a dedicated GitHub account/token for the skill so you can limit blast radius and rotate credentials easily. 4) Don’t store the token in a repository or publicly readable file; prefer a secrets manager or the OpenClaw secure config. 5) If you proceed, monitor the skill’s network requests (or run it in a sandbox) to confirm it only talks to api.github.com. If the maintainer cannot produce the missing api module or explain the discrepancy, do not install the skill.
